newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court grants EAGGF monies to Germany for bovine sector.
newsitem.headline: Court grants EAGGF monies to Germany for bovine sector.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday the European Agricultural Guidance and Guarantee Fund (EAGGF) should be charged for expenditures in 1990 relating to the beef and veal sectors in Germany.
The court annulled a Commission decision which said Germany did not apply the special premium scheme required by Community rules and therefore was not eligible for funds from the EAGGF.
The court reversed the decision in part only, finding Germany should receive DM 1,150,155, but not the DM 7,518,141 it sought.
The Commission found that Germany did not take adequate measures to prevent double payments of premiums. But the court noted that no provision of Community law then required such steps.
Furthermore, it said the coordination of national measures was a matter for Community institutions, not member states.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Clearance of accounts - EAGGF - Special premium for beef and veal producers - Expenditure disallowed"
Commission of the European Communities, defendant

application for the annulment of Commission decision 93/659/EC of 25 November 1993 on the clearance of the accounts presented by the member states in respect of the expenditure for 1990 of the European Agricultural Guidance and Guarantee Fund (EAGGF), Guarantee Section (OJ 1993 L 301, p. 13), to the extent to which it did not charge to the EAGGF the sum of DM 7,518,141 disbursed by the Federal Republic of Germany in relation to the Community scheme providing for a special premium for beef and veal producers.

1. Annuls Commission decision 93/659/EC of 25 November 1993 on the clearance of the accounts presented by the member states in respect of the expenditure for 1990 of the European Agricultural Guidance and Guarantee Fund (EAGGF), Guarantee Section, in so far as it did not charge to the EAGGF the sum of DM 838, 636 in respect of expenditure relating to the import into Germany of animals from Belgium and France and the sum of DM 311,529 in respect of expenditure relating to the export of animals to Italy;
2. Dismisses the remainder of the application;
3. Orders the parties to bear their own costs.
